record.summary: The first General Assembly resolution on regulating artificial intelligence. It calls on Member States and stakeholders to refrain from or cease using AI systems that cannot be operated in compliance with international human rights law or that pose undue risks to human rights, and affirms that the rights people have offline must also be protected online throughout the life cycle of AI systems. It urges States, the private sector, civil society, research organisations and the media to develop and support regulatory and governance approaches for safe, secure and trustworthy AI, and to help developing countries close the digital divide.
record.notes: Introduced by the United States and co-sponsored by more than 120 Member States; adopted without a vote on 21 March 2024. The second General Assembly resolution on AI that year, 78/311 of 1 July 2024 on capacity-building, is UN-03; both are recalled in resolution 79/325 of 26 August 2025 (UN-07).

verification.note: The resolution's own text could not be stored: the UN Digital Library record (official_url) returns a bot-check page, the press.un.org meeting coverage GA/12588 (the previous secondary_url) returns a JavaScript 'Client Challenge' page also in a browser, and documents.un.org is closed to automated downloads by robots.txt. Stored in this run instead, all from un.org hosts: the spokesperson's briefing of the President of the General Assembly of 21 March 2024 (title, adoption that morning, introduced by the United States, co-sponsored by over 120 Member States); the UN News article of 21 March 2024 (date, adoption without a vote, quotations of the operative text); the UN Photo caption of the adoption; A/RES/79/325, which recalls '78/265 of 21 March 2024'; and the High-level Advisory Body's final report, which names the resolution with its number. The summary is written from the operative text that UN News quotes. Version 1's meeting number, document date and the topics 'transparency & labelling' and 'accountability & liability' are not shown by any stored file and were removed; the UN News article is proposed as secondary_url because it can be stored and carries the content.

judgment.status_reasoning: Adopted without a vote on 21 March 2024 (UN News; the President's briefing says 'this morning' on 21 March 2024). Resolution 79/325 of 26 August 2025 recalls it among the Assembly's resolutions in effect, and no stored file shows a later resolution replacing it. A General Assembly resolution of this kind calls on States and does not bind them, so 'Published (non-binding, current)' and 'Non-binding' stand.
